summary: An excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (labeled 'Book 11 — part 45' in the note). Rebecca and uncle Jerry Cobb talk after a rain shower; Jane is described as a kind, gentler sister compared with the sharp Mirandy, and Rebecca reveals her wish to return to aunt Mirandy's house. Rebecca decides to go back despite fearing Mirandy may not take her in, and Jerry Cobb insists on helping her settle things.
one_line: Rebecca, after running away, resolves to return to aunt Mirandy's house while uncle Jerry Cobb offers to help her.
key_facts: Rebecca says aunt Jane is 'just as good and kind as she can be' and that she likes her better all the time.
Rebecca says aunt Jane 'can't stand up for me against aunt Mirandy; she's about as afraid of her as I am.'
Uncle Jerry asks whether Jane is 'a leetle bit more easy goin' than Mirandy' or 'jest as hard to please.'
Jane tells Sarah that she is keeping a sewing school and that her scholar has made three dresses.
Jane says she has taken a class in Sunday-school and means to go to the picnic with Rebecca.
Mother reports that Jane looked 'so young 'n' happy' after prayer meeting.
A rainbow appears through the window after the rain ceases, which Rebecca takes as a bridge over her troubles.
Uncle Jerry says the shower 'washed the face o' the airth nice an' clean' and that everything will shine tomorrow when he and Rebecca are driving up river.
Rebecca tells Mr. Cobb she is not going to drive up river and will instead go back.
Rebecca says she will 'catch bricks; catch 'em without throwing 'em back, too.'
Rebecca says she doesn't know if aunt Mirandy will take her in after she has run away.
Rebecca decides to return 'while I have the courage.'
Uncle Jerry declares he won't leave until he 'gits this thing fixed up.'
Uncle Jerry tells Rebecca she has had 'all you can stan' to-night' and expresses concern about her getting sick.
